# Model and source

* Citation: Bilous M, Serdjebi C, Boyer A, Tomasini P, Pouypoudat C,
  Barbolosi D, Barlesi F, Chomy F, Benzekry S. Quantitative mathematical
  modeling of clinical brain metastasis dynamics in non-small cell lung
  cancer. Sci Rep. 2019;9:13018.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-019-49407-3> (open access, with
  Supplementary Material: Table S1 and Figures S1-S9)

Bilous 2019 is a mechanistic disease model with no drug input. The primary
lung tumor grows from one cell by Gompertz kinetics until diagnosis, then
follows a tumor growth inhibition (TGI) model while the patient is on
systemic therapy. Brain metastases (BMs) are born at rate
`d(Sp) = mu * Sp^gamma` (the Iwata size-structured framework), so the
expected number born by time `t` is `N(t) = integral(mu * Sp^gamma)`. In the
selected *dormancy* model a newborn metastasis stays at one cell for `tau`
days and then grows by the untreated Gompertz law; metastases do not respond
to therapy. The number of metastases larger than a size `s` at time `t` is
then `N(t - t(s) - tau)`, where `t(s)` is the Gompertz time from one cell to
`s`.

The paper contributes four models:

| Model | Data | Role in the paper |
|-------|------|-------------------|
| `Bilous_2019_nsclc_bm_probability_adenocarcinoma` | Mujoomdar 2007, 136 adenocarcinoma patients | Population probability of BM at diagnosis (Figure 1A) |
| `Bilous_2019_nsclc_bm_probability_squamous` | Mujoomdar 2007, 47 squamous cell carcinoma patients | Population probability of BM at diagnosis (Figure 1B) |
| `Bilous_2019_nsclc_bm_dormancy_patient1` | Patient 1 (adenocarcinoma) | Individual fit of the dormancy model (Figures 2, 4, 5; Table 2) |
| `Bilous_2019_nsclc_bm_dormancy_patient2` | Patient 2 (squamous cell carcinoma) | Individual fit of the dormancy model (Figures S7, S8; Table 2) |

The four candidate metastasis models that the dormancy model was selected
over (basic, different growth, secondary dissemination and delay; Table 1 and
Figures S3-S6) are not packaged.

All four models run on a time axis in days from the first cancer cell
(`t = 0`), because the dormancy model needs the number of metastases born
before diagnosis. The diagnosis time `td` is computed inside each model from
the primary tumor diameter at diagnosis (covariate `TUMSZ`, mm) and is
returned as an output column, together with `time_after_diag = t - td` in the
patient-level models.

# Population

The population-level models were fitted to the brain-metastasis frequency by
primary tumor size reported by Mujoomdar et al. (Radiology 2007;242:882) for
136 adenocarcinoma and 47 squamous cell carcinoma patients, taken from the
literature. The individual-level models were each fitted to one patient with
unresectable NSCLC: patient 1 had an EGFR-mutated adenocarcinoma (Institut
Bergonie, Bordeaux; 10 primary tumor and 47 brain-metastasis size
measurements over 6 MRI time points, treated with erlotinib, docetaxel, an
erlotinib re-challenge and gemcitabine) and patient 2 had an EGFR wild-type
squamous cell carcinoma (University Hospital of Marseille; 11 primary tumor and
16 brain-metastasis size measurements over 4 MRI time points). The paper gives
no demographics. The same information is in each model's `population`
metadata (`readModelDb("Bilous_2019_nsclc_bm_dormancy_patient1")()$population`).

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. They are
collected here.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Gompertz primary tumor growth before diagnosis | `dSp/dt = (alpha0p - betap ln Sp) Sp`, `Sp(0) = 1` | Materials and Methods, Primary tumor growth |
| TGI after diagnosis (equation 1) | `dSp/dt = alpha1 Sp - kappa exp(-(t - Td) ln2 / t_res) Sp` | Materials and Methods, equation 1 |
| Dissemination rate (equation 2) | `d = mu Sp^gamma` | Materials and Methods, equation 2 |
| Number of metastases (equation 4) | `N(t) = integral_0^t d(Sp)` | Materials and Methods, equation 4 |
| Dormancy model | `f_dorm(t, s) = N(t - t(s) - tau)`, `t(s) = -ln(1 - beta/alpha0 ln s)/beta` | Materials and Methods, Dormancy model and equation 5 |
| Gompertz calibration | `exp(alpha0p/betap) = 1e12`, doubling-time equation for `DT(Sd)` | Materials and Methods, Pre-clinical primary tumor growth |
| `ltsmax` | `log(1e12)` (fixed) | Methods, carrying capacity 10^12 cells |
| `cell_density` | 1e6 cells/mm^3 (fixed) | Methods, '1 mm3 = 10^6 cells' |
| `tdouble` adenocarcinoma | 201 day (fixed) | Supplementary Table S1 average; Methods text |
| `tdouble` squamous | 104 day (fixed) | Supplementary Table S1 average |
| `diam_ref` (population models) | 35 mm (fixed) | Results, 'diameter 35 mm (median value from ref.50)' |
| `gamma` | 1 (fixed) | Table 2 (both patients); Methods, Population level 'set gamma = 1' |
| `diam_vis` patient 1 | 3 mm (fixed) | Table 2 'Visibility threshold'; Figure 5A |
| `diam_vis` patient 2 | 5 mm (fixed) | Methods 'S_vis ... 5 mm'; Figure S7A bins (Table 2 prints 3 mm; see Assumptions) |
| `lp` (alpha1) patient 1 / 2 | 5.72e-4 / 0.0101 1/day | Table 2 |
| `lkkill` (kappa) patient 1 / 2 | 4.46e-3 / 0.0439 1/day | Table 2 |
| `lthalf_res` (t_res) patient 1 / 2 | 149 / 35.4 day | Table 2 |
| `lmu` patient 1 / 2 | 2.00e-12 / 1.02e-12 1/(cell day) | Table 2 |
| `ltau_dorm` patient 1 / 2 | 133 / 171 day | Table 2 |
| `addSd_metastases_visible` patient 1 / 2 | 0.3347 / 0.3627 | Table 1 dormancy SSE 4.93 / 1.71, `sqrt(SSE / (N - P))` with N = 47 / 16, P = 3 |
| `lmu`, `etalmu` adenocarcinoma | median 1.56e-13, omega^2 8.982 | Figure 1A legend mu_pop = 1.39e-11, mu_sigma = 1.24e-9 (mean and SD) |
| `lmu`, `etalmu` squamous | median 2.79e-15, omega^2 8.289 | Figure 1B legend mu_pop = 1.76e-13, mu_sigma = 1.11e-11 (mean and SD) |

```{r load-models}
mod_p1 <- readModelDb("Bilous_2019_nsclc_bm_dormancy_patient1")
mod_p2 <- readModelDb("Bilous_2019_nsclc_bm_dormancy_patient2")
mod_adeno <- readModelDb("Bilous_2019_nsclc_bm_probability_adenocarcinoma")
mod_squam <- readModelDb("Bilous_2019_nsclc_bm_probability_squamous")

par_of <- function(mod, name) {
  ini_df <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$iniDf
  ini_df$est[ini_df$name == name]
}

days_per_month <- 365.25 / 12
```

# Patient-level dormancy models

## Solving the models

Each patient is solved on a one-day grid from the first cancer cell to 50
months after diagnosis. The observation rows are on the
`metastases_visible` state; `tumor`, `metastases` and the derived outputs
(`tumor_diam`, `td`, `alpha_gomp`, `beta_gomp`) come back as columns.

```{r solve-patients}
solve_patient <- function(mod, tumsz, months_after = 50) {
  ev0 <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "metastases_visible", TUMSZ = tumsz)
  td <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev0, returnType = "data.frame")$td[1]
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = 1L,
    time = sort(unique(c(seq(0, ceiling(td + months_after * days_per_month), by = 1), td))),
    evid = 0L,
    cmt = "metastases_visible",
    TUMSZ = tumsz
  )
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-10, maxsteps = 1e6)
  sim$month <- sim$time_after_diag / days_per_month
  sim
}

sim_p1 <- solve_patient(mod_p1, tumsz = 36.0)
sim_p2 <- solve_patient(mod_p2, tumsz = 53.7)
```

## Discrete brain metastases

The paper simulates individual metastases with a discrete version of the
model (Methods, Discrete versions of the models): the i-th metastasis is born
at `T_i = inf{t : N(t) >= i}`, stays at one cell for `tau` and then grows by
the Gompertz law. The helper below reconstructs these lesions from the solved
`N(t)`.

```{r discrete-bms}
bm_lesions <- function(sim, mod) {
  n_max <- floor(max(sim$metastases))
  birth <- stats::approx(sim$metastases, sim$time, xout = seq_len(n_max), ties = "ordered")$y
  data.frame(
    bm = seq_len(n_max),
    birth = birth,
    tau = exp(par_of(mod, "ltau_dorm")),
    alpha = sim$alpha_gomp[1],
    beta = sim$beta_gomp[1],
    td = sim$td[1],
    density = par_of(mod, "cell_density")
  )
}

bm_size_cells <- function(lesions, t) {
  grow <- pmax(t - lesions$birth - lesions$tau, 0)
  size <- exp(lesions$alpha / lesions$beta * (1 - exp(-lesions$beta * grow)))
  ifelse(t >= lesions$birth, size, NA_real_)
}

cells_to_mm <- function(cells, density = 1e6) (6 * cells / (pi * density))^(1 / 3)

les_p1 <- bm_lesions(sim_p1, mod_p1)
les_p2 <- bm_lesions(sim_p2, mod_p2)
```

## Patient 1: diagnosis-time predictions (Table 2 and Results)

```{r p1-claims}
at <- function(sim, month, col) stats::approx(sim$month, sim[[col]], xout = month)$y
first_month <- function(sim, col, k = 1) min(sim$month[sim[[col]] >= k])

td1 <- sim_p1$td[1]
size_td1 <- bm_size_cells(les_p1, td1)
first_vis1 <- first_month(sim_p1, "metastases_visible")
# T2 = 19 months, the model-predicted first visible BM in the Results; the
# packaged parameters (rounded to three figures) put it at 19.7 months.
t2_1 <- td1 + 19 * days_per_month
size_t2_1 <- bm_size_cells(les_p1, t2_1)
s30 <- 1e6 * pi / 6 * 30^3
dt30 <- function(sim) {
  a <- sim$alpha_gomp[1]
  b <- sim$beta_gomp[1]
  -log((b * log(2 * s30) - a) / (b * log(s30) - a)) / b
}

claims_p1 <- data.frame(
  quantity = c(
    "Age of the primary tumor at diagnosis (year)",
    "alpha0p (1/day)",
    "betap (1/day)",
    "PT doubling time at 3 cm (day)",
    "Dissemination rate at 3 cm (1/day)",
    "BMs present at diagnosis",
    "BM burden at diagnosis (cells)",
    "Largest BM at diagnosis (cells)",
    "First BM birth (months after diagnosis)",
    "First BM visible (months after diagnosis)",
    "BMs present at T2 = 19 months",
    "Dormancy duration (months)"
  ),
  paper = c(5.3, 0.0284, 1.03e-3, 173, 0.0282, 10, 1167, 1046, -14, 19, 28, 4.4),
  model = c(
    td1 / 365.25,
    sim_p1$alpha_gomp[1],
    sim_p1$beta_gomp[1],
    dt30(sim_p1),
    exp(par_of(mod_p1, "lmu")) * s30^par_of(mod_p1, "gamma"),
    floor(at(sim_p1, 0, "metastases")),
    sum(size_td1, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(size_td1, na.rm = TRUE),
    (les_p1$birth[1] - td1) / days_per_month,
    first_vis1,
    sum(!is.na(size_t2_1)),
    les_p1$tau[1] / days_per_month
  ),
  source = c(
    "Table 2 T_d", "Table 2", "Table 2", "Table 2 DT_PT", "Table 2 d",
    "Results ('10 occult BMs')", "Results ('1,167 cells')", "Results ('1,046 cells')",
    "Results ('14 months before')", "Results; Figure 4C ('19 vs 20 months')",
    "Results ('28 tumors')", "Discussion ('4.4 ... months')"
  )
)
claims_p1$pct_diff <- 100 * (claims_p1$model / claims_p1$paper - 1)
show_claims <- function(tab) {
  tab |>
    mutate(across(c(paper, model), function(x) formatC(x, digits = 4, format = "g"))) |>
    knitr::kable(digits = 2)
}
show_claims(claims_p1)
```

Every reported quantity is reproduced to within a few percent, the
rounding of the printed parameters; the first visible metastasis comes 0.7
months after the reported 19 months. The model gives `r formatC(sum(size_t2_1, na.rm = TRUE), format = "e", digits = 1)`
cells of total BM burden at T2 (19 months), against 1.7e7 in the Results.

```{r p1-assert}
# The model is deterministic and these quantities follow from the printed
# (rounded) parameters. 3% admits the rounding of alpha0p, betap and mu to
# three significant figures; a wrong doubling time, carrying capacity, cell
# density or unit moves them by tens of percent.
stopifnot(
  nrow(claims_p1) == 12L,
  all(abs(claims_p1$pct_diff[1:5]) < 3),
  claims_p1$model[6] == 10,
  abs(claims_p1$model[7] / 1167 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(claims_p1$model[8] / 1046 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(claims_p1$model[9] - (-14)) < 1,
  abs(claims_p1$model[10] - 19) < 1,
  abs(claims_p1$model[11] - 28) <= 2,
  abs(sum(size_t2_1, na.rm = TRUE) / 1.7e7 - 1) < 0.1
)
```

## Patient 1: primary tumor during treatment (Figure 2A)

```{r p1-fig2a}
sim_p1 |>
  filter(month >= 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(month, tumor_diam)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    x = "Months after diagnosis", y = "Primary tumor diameter (mm)",
    caption = "Replicates the TGI fit line of Figure 2A of Bilous 2019."
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 40))
```

The fitted line of Figure 2A starts at 36 mm, reaches a nadir of about 30 mm
around 15 to 20 months and returns to about 35 mm at 48 months.

```{r p1-fig2a-assert}
nadir_p1 <- sim_p1 |> filter(month >= 0, month <= 48)
stopifnot(
  abs(at(sim_p1, 0, "tumor_diam") - 36) < 0.1,
  abs(min(nadir_p1$tumor_diam) - 30) < 1.5,
  abs(at(sim_p1, 48, "tumor_diam") - 35) < 1.5
)
c(diagnosis = at(sim_p1, 0, "tumor_diam"), nadir = min(nadir_p1$tumor_diam), month48 = at(sim_p1, 48, "tumor_diam"))
```

## Patient 1: number of visible brain metastases (Figure 4)

The model bars of Figure 4A give the number of visible metastases (3 mm or
larger) at each MRI; the observed counts are those of Figure 2C. Both were
read off the figures by the maintainers.

```{r p1-fig4}
fig4 <- data.frame(
  month = c(19, 23, 28, 40, 43, 48),
  paper_model = c(0, 1, 4, 17, 19, 23),
  observed = c(1, 1, 1, 6, 18, 20)
)
fig4$model_continuous <- at(sim_p1, fig4$month, "metastases_visible")
fig4$model_discrete <- vapply(
  fig4$month,
  function(m) sum(cells_to_mm(bm_size_cells(les_p1, td1 + m * days_per_month)) >= 3, na.rm = TRUE),
  numeric(1)
)
knitr::kable(fig4, digits = 2)

sim_p1 |>
  filter(month >= 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(month, metastases_visible)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig4, aes(month, observed), colour = "grey40", shape = 8, size = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Months after diagnosis", y = "Number of visible metastases",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4B of Bilous 2019 (line: model; stars: observed, Figure 2C)."
  )
```

```{r p1-fig4-assert}
# The discrete count is floor(N(t - t_vis - tau)), so it must equal the
# floor of the continuous visible-count state exactly (up to a solver
# rounding at an integer crossing).
stopifnot(
  all(abs(fig4$model_discrete - floor(fig4$model_continuous + 1e-6)) <= 1),
  all(abs(fig4$model_discrete - fig4$paper_model) <= 2)
)
```

## Patient 1: natural history of the disease (Figure 5)

```{r p1-fig5, fig.height = 5}
grid_t <- seq(les_p1$birth[1], td1 + 48 * days_per_month, length.out = 400)
bm_paths <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(les_p1)), function(i) {
  sz <- bm_size_cells(les_p1[i, ], grid_t)
  data.frame(bm = i, month = (grid_t - td1) / days_per_month, cells = sz)
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  filter(!is.na(cells)) |>
  group_by(bm) |>
  filter(max(cells) >= 1e6 * pi / 6 * 3^3) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = filter(sim_p1, month <= 48), aes(month, tumor), colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(data = bm_paths, aes(month, cells, group = bm), colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1e6 * pi / 6 * 3^3, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Months after diagnosis", y = "Tumor size (cells)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5A of Bilous 2019 (blue: primary tumor; red: brain metastases that become visible)."
  )
```

All eight metastases present at diagnosis are still dormant single cells, as
the Results state. The first one is born
`r round((les_p2$birth[1] - td2) / days_per_month, 1)` months before
diagnosis, which matches the earliest initiation time in Figure S8B (about
-5.5 months); the Results text says "45 months prior to diagnosis", which
cannot hold for a primary tumor that is 2.1 years (25 months) old at
diagnosis and is taken to be a misprint for 4.5 months.

The steps of the visible-count curve in Figure S7B (model line, 5 mm
threshold) were read off the figure by the maintainers.

# Population models: probability of brain metastasis at diagnosis (Figure 1)

The probability that a patient whose primary tumor has diameter `D` at
diagnosis already has a brain metastasis is `P(N(td) > 1)`, with `mu`
log-normal between patients. Because `N(td)` is proportional to `mu`, the
probability follows in closed form from one typical-value solve per diameter,
`P = 1 - Phi(-log(N_typical(td)) / omega)`; a stochastic check on 200 virtual
patients per histology confirms the closed form.

```{r pop-typical}
solve_n_at_td <- function(mod, diam_mm) {
  ev0 <- data.frame(id = seq_along(diam_mm), time = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "metastases", TUMSZ = diam_mm)
  td <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev0, omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame")$td
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = rep(seq_along(diam_mm), each = 2),
    time = as.vector(rbind(0, td)),
    evid = 0L,
    cmt = "metastases",
    TUMSZ = rep(diam_mm, each = 2)
  )
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)
  # rxSolve omits the id column when the event table has a single subject.
  if (!"id" %in% names(sim)) sim$id <- 1L
  sim |>
    group_by(id) |>
    slice_tail(n = 1) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(TUMSZ = diam_mm, td = td)
}

prob_curve <- function(mod, diam_mm) {
  ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
  om <- sqrt(ui$omega["etalmu", "etalmu"])
  typ <- solve_n_at_td(mod, diam_mm)
  # The typical solve uses mu = exp(lmu), so N(td) = exp(lmu) * I(td) with
  # I(td) the integral of the tumor size. For log(mu) ~ N(lmu, om^2),
  # P(mu * I(td) > 1) = 1 - Phi((-log(I(td)) - lmu) / om)
  #                   = 1 - Phi(-log(N_typical(td)) / om).
  typ$prob <- 1 - stats::pnorm(-log(typ$metastases) / om)
  typ
}

diam_grid <- seq(5, 90, by = 1)
curve_adeno <- prob_curve(mod_adeno, diam_grid) |> mutate(histology = "Adenocarcinoma")
curve_squam <- prob_curve(mod_squam, diam_grid) |> mutate(histology = "Squamous cell carcinoma")
curves <- bind_rows(curve_adeno, curve_squam)
```

The model curves of Figure 1 were digitised by the maintainers from the
figure pixels; the Mujoomdar 2007 data points were read off the same figure.

```{r pop-fig1}
fig1_model <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    histology = "Adenocarcinoma",
    D_cm = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9),
    paper_pct = c(5.5, 20.5, 38.5, 51.7, 63.5, 71.0, 78.0, 83.0, 88.0)
  ),
  data.frame(
    histology = "Squamous cell carcinoma",
    D_cm = c(2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8),
    paper_pct = c(2.0, 4.5, 8.5, 12.5, 20.3, 27.2, 34.8)
  )
)
fig1_data <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(histology = "Adenocarcinoma", D_cm = c(1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 5.5, 7.5), pct = c(25, 41, 29, 76, 44, 79)),
  data.frame(histology = "Squamous cell carcinoma", D_cm = c(1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 5.5, 7.5), pct = c(0, 9, 0, 9, 20, 33))
)
fig1_model$model_pct <- mapply(
  function(h, d) 100 * curves$prob[curves$histology == h & curves$TUMSZ == round(10 * d)],
  fig1_model$histology, fig1_model$D_cm
)
fig1_model$diff_pct_points <- fig1_model$model_pct - fig1_model$paper_pct
knitr::kable(fig1_model, digits = 1)

ggplot(curves, aes(TUMSZ / 10, 100 * prob)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = fig1_model, aes(D_cm, paper_pct), shape = 3) +
  geom_point(data = fig1_data, aes(D_cm, pct), colour = "darkorange", shape = 1, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~histology) +
  labs(
    x = "Primary tumor diameter (cm)", y = "Metastasis probability (%)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of Bilous 2019 (line: model; crosses: published model curve; circles: Mujoomdar 2007 data)."
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100))
```

```{r pop-fig1-assert}
adeno_rows <- fig1_model$histology == "Adenocarcinoma"
stopifnot(
  sum(adeno_rows) == 9L,
  # Adenocarcinoma reproduces the published curve within 2.5 percentage points.
  all(abs(fig1_model$diff_pct_points[adeno_rows]) < 2.5),
  # Squamous runs 1 to 7 points below the published curve (see Assumptions);
  # the gate keeps it within 10 points so a wrong doubling time or mu fails.
  all(abs(fig1_model$diff_pct_points[!adeno_rows]) < 10)
)
```

## Stochastic check (200 virtual patients per histology)

```{r pop-stochastic}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190911)
n_sub <- 200L
check_prob <- function(mod, diam_mm, label) {
  td <- solve_n_at_td(mod, diam_mm)$td
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = rep(seq_len(n_sub), each = 2),
    time = rep(c(0, td), n_sub),
    evid = 0L,
    cmt = "metastases",
    TUMSZ = diam_mm
  )
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  at_td <- sim |> filter(abs(time - td) < 1e-8)
  data.frame(
    histology = label,
    TUMSZ = diam_mm,
    simulated = mean(at_td$bm_present),
    closed_form = curves$prob[curves$histology == label & curves$TUMSZ == diam_mm],
    n = nrow(at_td)
  )
}
stoch <- bind_rows(
  check_prob(mod_adeno, 40, "Adenocarcinoma"),
  check_prob(mod_squam, 80, "Squamous cell carcinoma")
)
knitr::kable(stoch, digits = 3)
# Binomial SE at n = 200 is at most 0.035; 0.15 is more than 4 SE, and a
# mis-specified omega (for example the SD read as a log-scale SD) moves the
# probability by more than 0.3.
stopifnot(all(stoch$n == n_sub), all(abs(stoch$simulated - stoch$closed_form) < 0.15))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Time axis.** All models run from the first cancer cell. The diagnosis
  time `td` is not a parameter: it is computed from the diameter at
  diagnosis (`TUMSZ`) on the Gompertz curve, and the treatment effect in the
  patient-level models switches on at `td`. Users simulate past `td` and read
  `time_after_diag` (patient models) or evaluate the population models at
  `t = td`.
* **Gompertz parameters are computed, not tabulated.** The Methods doubling-time
  equation has a closed-form solution once `alpha0p = betap * log(1e12)`, so
  each model computes `alpha0p` and `betap` from the doubling time and the
  calibration diameter. For the two patients this reproduces the Table 2
  "Computed" values (0.0284 and 1.03e-3; 0.0858 and 3.10e-3 per day).
* **Squamous doubling time.** The Methods text gives 104 days for "an
  undifferentiated carcinoma", but Supplementary Table S1 gives 104 days as
  the squamous cell carcinoma average (91 days for undifferentiated
  carcinoma). 104 days reproduces Table 2 for the squamous patient, so it is
  used for squamous cell carcinoma.
* **Population mu distribution.** The Methods write
  `ln(mu) ~ N(ln(mu_pop), mu_sigma)` and call `mu_pop` the median, but
  `mu_sigma` (1.24e-9 and 1.11e-11) carries the units of `mu` and the text
  reports coefficients of variation above 6000%, which is `mu_sigma / mu_pop`
  (8921% and 6307%). Read as a log-scale SD, `mu_sigma` would remove all
  variability; read with `mu_pop` as the median, the probability would exceed
  50% at every diameter, contradicting Figure 1. Reading `mu_pop` and
  `mu_sigma` as the mean and SD of the log-normal `mu` reproduces Figure 1A
  to within 2.5 percentage points, so `lmu` is the log median
  `log(mu_pop) - omega^2 / 2` with `omega^2 = log(1 + (mu_sigma / mu_pop)^2)`.
* **Population growth calibration diameter.** The Methods fix the primary
  tumor growth parameters "from the cohort histology" without naming the
  diameter at which the doubling time applies. The models use 35 mm, the
  median diameter the Results quote from the same data source; calibrating
  at each patient's own diameter instead gives 72% rather than 88% at 9 cm
  for adenocarcinoma. No squamous-specific diameter is printed and 35 mm is
  used for both histologies. The squamous curve then runs 1 to 7 percentage
  points below Figure 1B (35% against about 40% at 8.5-9 cm); this deviation
  is reported, not tuned.
* **Visibility threshold for patient 2.** Table 2 prints 3 mm for both
  patients, while the Methods define the visible size as 5 mm. Patient 1's
  results (first visible metastasis at 19 months; Figure 4A bins from 3 mm)
  need 3 mm. Patient 2's fit (Figure S7A bins from 5 mm) needs 5 mm: with
  5 mm the visible-count steps of Figure S7B are reproduced within 0.6 months,
  with 3 mm each comes about 1.5 months early. Patient 2 therefore uses 5 mm.
* **Residual error.** The paper fits the number of metastases larger than
  each observed size with `y = f + sigma * eps` and estimates sigma a
  posteriori as `l(theta) / (N - P)`, which it uses as a variance in its
  covariance formula. The additive SD is therefore
  `sqrt(SSE / (N - P))` from the Table 1 dormancy objective (4.93 with 47
  points for patient 1; 1.71 with 16 points for patient 2; P = 3 parameters
  `mu`, `tau`, `gamma`). It is attached to the visible-count output, which is
  the cumulative size distribution at the visibility threshold. The paper
  does not report the error model of the primary tumor TGI fit, so no
  primary-tumor endpoint carries residual error; `tumor_diam` is an output
  only.
* **Observation name.** `metastases_visible` is not a registered output
  name, so the convention check reports it for the two patient-level
  models; there is no canonical output for a count of metastases.
* **Cumulative size distributions.** The model returns `N(t)` and the
  visible count; counts above any other size `s` are
  `N(t - t(s) - tau)` and are computed from the solved `N(t)` as in this
  article.
* **Not packaged.** The basic, different-growth, secondary-dissemination
  and delay models were candidates the dormancy model was selected over
  (Table 1; Figures S3-S6). The secondary-dissemination model has no closed
  `N(t)` and was fitted with a dedicated characteristics scheme.
* **No erratum.** No correction to Bilous 2019 is registered in Crossref or
  Europe PMC (checked 2026-11-25).
* **No NCA.** The models have no drug and no concentration, so the
  validation uses the paper's reported disease-course predictions instead of
  PKNCA.
